newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul's steps expected to attract $8 bln in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Seoul's steps expected to attract $8 bln in 1997.

text.p: The Seoul government's measures to expand overseas borrowings and speed up the liberalisation of the local capital market are expected to attract an additional $8 billion in 1997, a finance ministry official said on Monday.
The official said that a total of $28 billion of foreign capital is now expected to flow into the country this year, instead of an earlier estimate of $20 billion.

The official, who asked not to be identified, said state banks would seek an additional $1 billion in overseas loans this year while locally-based foreign manufacturers were expected to raise their borrowings by $2 billion.
Earlier on Monday, the ministry said it would allow the foreign manufacturers to freely borrow loans abroad if the money was to be used for operating funds.

As part of measures to encourage the inflow of foreign capital to stop a fall in the local currency, South Korea also raised the foreign stock ownership ceiling to 23 percent from the current 20 percent, effective from May 1.
The official estimated that the foreign shareownership expansion would lead to an inflow of another $3 billion in foreign funds.

The government would also allow local financial institutions to raise about $200 million each in Asia and in Europe to launch funds specialising in investment in the domestic bond market this year. No other details were given.
